Axios Pro Rata
By Dan Primack · Sep 03, 2026
 
 
Top of the Morning
 

Photo illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Photos: European/FPG/Archive Photos, Andrew Harnik and Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images
 

Defense tech has become one of venture capital's hottest sectors, after being ignored for decades, but it just lost a top evangelist within the Pentagon.

Driving the news: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll this week resigned, after clashing with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

  • It follows Hegseth's firing of Gen. Randy George, the Army's chief of staff, and many other forced departures across most services.
  • The Army is now without its top two Senate-confirmed leaders, despite the ongoing Iran conflict.

Behind the scenes: Driscoll was viewed as tech's top military man in D.C.

  • He had spent a few years as COO of venture firm Flex Capital, and had pledged to bring a "Silicon Valley" ethos to procurement and deployment.
  • He and George also supported the Army Transformation Initiative, which would have eliminated certain big-name and big-cost weapons — believing that drones had fundamentally changed the future of warfare.
  • But Driscoll's focus on modernization was in conflict with Hegseth, who reportedly was more concerned about culture war issues like eliminating DEI initiatives.
  • After his firing, George joined a venture capital firm.

Vibes check: Defense-tech investors tell me that they're concerned and disappointed, but not slowing down.

  • "Driscoll is very widely respected across the defense sector generally and the defense-tech world specifically [but] on the substance I don't think anything changes," one tells me. "Momentum is bigger than any one person."
  • There's also a pervasive sentiment that Driscoll could be back at DoD, perhaps as secretary, were Vice President JD Vance to become president. The two are close friends and former classmates at Yale Law School — a relationship that may have contributed to Hegseth's "suspicious and paranoid" attitude toward his Army chief.

By the numbers: U.S. defense-tech companies have raised $51.1 billion so far this year, per PitchBook, compared to $52.4 billion for all of 2025.

  • For context, there was less than $7 billion invested in 2016.

The bottom line: So long as DoD budgets remain robust, capital will flow. Even if the path has become a bit bumpier.
 
 
The BFD
 

Illustration: Shoshana Gordon/Axios
 

Nvidia (Nasdaq: NVDA) announced that it will acquire open-source AI platform Hugging Face for $12.93 billion.

Why it's the BFD: This is a massive validation of open-source AI, by a chip design giant known for its work with closed-model companies like Anthropic and OpenAI.

  • It also comes just a month after Hugging Face was hacked by OpenAI models gone rogue, in what's become a major security wakeup call for the industry.

ROI: Hugging Face had raised around $400 million in VC funding, most recently at a $4.5 billion valuation in 2023.

  • Backers include Lux Capital, Addition, Sequoia Capital, Coatue, Menlo Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, and Nvidia.

Flashback: I interviewed Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue at last year's Axios BFD event. Here's the video.

Behind the scenes: Hugging Face approached Nvidia about a deal, but had other bidders.

  • In addition to the purchase price, Nvidia will pay up to $1 billion in employee retention bonuses.

The bottom line: "This is another example of Nvidia's longer term goal: to be the top open AI model player. In the release, Nvidia emphasized Hugging Face's role in supporting open weight AI models, or those models with weights that are public and can be tinkered with by the end user." — Madison Mills, Axios
 
 
Venture Capital Deals
 

• Wonderful, a Dutch enterprise AI deployment company, raised $550m at a $5b valuation. Insight Partners led, joined by Salesforce and insiders Index Ventures, IVP, Vine Ventures, 9Yards, and Bessemer Venture Partners. axios.link/4gNlaxQ

• Upwind, an Israeli cloud security company, raised $300m at a $3.8b valuation. Bessemer Venture Partners and TCV led, joined by Craft Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, Greylock, Cyberstarts, Leaders Fund, Alta Park Capital, and Penny Jar Capital. axios.link/4x8TZ6x

• Medici Brands, the parent company of David Protein and confectionery brand HallPass, raised $250m at a $2.25b post-money valuation. Greenoaks led, joined by Valor Equity Partners, Iconiq, and Imaginary Ventures. axios.link/4x2feH8

• Lyte, a Sunnyvale, Calif.-based robotics and AI startup, raised a $165m Series C at a $1.6b post-money valuation. Maverick Silicon led, joined by Fidelity, Atreides Management, Key1 Capital, and Ora Global. axios.link/4x26AZi

• iPronics, a Spanish provider of optical networking solutions for AI infrastructure, raised $125m in Series B funding. Maverick Silicon and Light Street Capital led, joined by Nvidia, Triatomic Capital, Bosch Ventures, Catalight Capital, European Innovation Council Fund, Tate Family Trust, Fine Structure Ventures, Amadeus Capital Partners, Build Collective, and Criteria Venture Tech. axios.link/4x8EWtV

🚑 Thyme Care, a Nashville, Tenn.-based cancer care company, raised $125m in Series E funding at a $2b+ valuation. Morgan Health led, joined by Humana, CVS Health Ventures, AlleyCorp, HealthQuest Capital, Foresite Capital, Concord Health Partners, Frist Cressey Ventures, Town Hall Ventures, and a16z. axios.link/4iJegMz

• HiddenLayer, an Austin, Texas-based enterprise AI security startup, raised $100m in Series B funding. Delta-v Capital led, joined by Ten Eleven Ventures, M12, Microsoft's venture fund, Morgan Stanley, and Booz Allen Ventures. axios.link/4wYRxQ5

🚑 PatientIQ, a Chicago-based patient outcomes data company, raised $30m in Series C funding, per Axios Pro. Hughes & Co. led, joined by insider Health Enterprise Partners. axios.link/4h7o7dN

• Aslan, a maker of AI agents that act as operatives in national security missions, raised $20.8m. Khosla Ventures and XYZ Venture Capital led, joined by 2048 Ventures, BoxGroup, Liquid2, and Alumni Ventures. axios.link/4clokaO

• Atira, a German AI sales engineering platform, raised $17.5m led by Accel, with participation from UVC, Fortino, and Booom. axios.link/4ctvh9D

• Critical Materials Group, an Austin-based explosives manufacturing startup, raised $10.3m in seed funding. Overmatch Ventures led, joined by Victory Six Advisors, and Fulcrum Ventures. axios.link/4qU0YyW

• Konko AI, a patient coordination platform focused on Latin America, raised $6m led by Hi Ventures. axios.link/4irBKpB

• Zeit AI, a German developer of autonomous data engineering tech, raised €5m from YC, University of Oxford's Seed Fund, Sequoia Capital Scout Fund, ACE Ventures and Hasso Plattner VC. axios.link/4cr1COs

• Backbone, a Belgian food quality and compliance platform, raised €4m in pre-seed funding. Pitchdrive led, joined by PROfounders Capital, Passion Capital, 100IN, Agristo, and Darta. axios.link/4gLZMZA

• Plenti, a Colombian fintech focused on currency movement and investment services, raised $3m in seed funding. Tether led, joined by Verda Ventures. axios.link/4x0ZdBh

• Apax Digital invested in Wematch, an Israeli platform for securities finance and capital markets workflows. axios.link/4gzPqgI

• Aquiline agreed to acquire a control stake in wealthtech platform Flourish, from MassMutual (which retains a stake). axios.link/464jo6t

• Bridgepoint acquired a majority stake in VIPR Solutions, a London-based tech platform for delegated authority intelligence. axios.link/4xx47Hl

• Enstructure, owned by V12 Partners, acquired the marine services unit of Logistec, a portfolio company of Blue Wolf Capital Partners, Investissement Québec, Yellow Point Equity Partners, and Stonepeak. axios.link/46AQ7jU

• GreenArrow, a CAI Capital portfolio company, acquired MSL Electric, an Anaheim, Calif.-based electrical contractor. axios.link/4yfOZhs

🚑 H.I.G. Capital acquired Outcomes One, an Orlando, Fla.-based provider of clinical network services and pharmacy tech. axios.link/4xzGwG7

• La Caisse is investing $1.3b for a 24% stake in Altius, a Brookfield-backed operator of telecom towers in India. axios.link/3T7922Q

• Marco Sealing Solutions, backed by Align Capital Partners, acquired Global O-Ring and Seal, a Houston-based distributor of industrial sealing products. axios.link/4634SMq

• NetSPI, a KKR-backed penetration testing firm, is merging with continuous security simulation startup Synack, per Axios Pro. Synack has raised more than $100m from VC firms like M12, Kleiner Perkins, Notable Capital, GV, and B Capital. axios.link/4yd4jLS

• Officine Maccaferri, an Ambienta portfolio company, acquired Ovattificio Alpino, an Italian provider of non-woven geotextiles and technical felts. axios.link/4zQ1pyg

• Pivotal, a Pollen Street Capital portfolio company, acquired LR Finance, a U.K. mortgage and protection brokerage. axios.link/4h6DZx7

• Proofpoint, a Thoma Bravo portfolio company, reportedly is in talks to buy cybersecurity firm Varonis Systems (Nasdaq: VRNS), which has around a $5.4b market cap. axios.link/4yh6E8w

🌏 Reworld Waste, backed by EQT and GIC, acquired three environmental solutions companies: Clean & Green Recycling, ClearFlo Technologies and EnviroTec. axios.link/4zQiJDc

• Sandberg Capital acquired a majority stake in Carrot, a Polish B2B vehicle auctions platform. axios.link/4xDyfkD

• Trafera, an ed-tech portfolio company of Rotunda Capital Partners, acquired Morris Electronics, a Morris, Minn.-based IT company. axios.link/4xCGVHZ

• Trimlite, a Wynnchurch Capital portfolio company, acquired Lexington, Ky.-based KW Building Products from Clay-Ingels. axios.link/4zYUqDp

🚑 West Physics Consulting, an Incline Equity Partners portfolio company, acquired Radiographic Testing Services, an Albany, N.Y.-based medical equipment services provider. axios.link/4x9uH8H
 
 
Public Offerings
 

• Accelevation, a Miamisburg, Ohio-based provider of power distribution and other data center infrastructure, filed for an IPO that Renaissance Capital estimates could raise $800m. It was acquired last year by Olympus Partners and plans to list on the Nasdaq (ACCV). axios.link/3UUZPuZ

• Hotel Investment Partners, a Spanish hotel operator owned by Blackstone, is planning to go public this fall, per Cinco Dias. axios.link/4cpcaxs
 
 
Liquidity Events
 

• Adobe (Nasdaq: ADBE) acquired Rilo, an Indian marketing intelligence startup seeded by Peak XV, DeVC, and Day Zero Ventures. axios.link/4gt7adG

• Barilla Group agreed to acquire Goodles, a mac-and-cheese brand that raised around $23m from firms like L Catterton and Springdale Ventures. axios.link/4gHl22M

🚑 Cerebral, a venture-backed tele-behavioral company, is seeking a buyer, per Axios Pro. It raised $462m in VC funding, including at a $4.8b valuation in 2021, from firms like SoftBank, Prysm Capital, Access Industries, WestCap Group, and ARTIS Ventures. axios.link/4ifApC9

⚡ Diversified Energy (NYSE: DEC) agreed to acquire Birch Resources, a Permian-focused oil and gas company, for $1.8b from Elliott Investment Management. axios.link/4yjDTrX

• Fort Point Capital is seeking to sell AMS Fulfillment Holdings, a Valencia, Calif.-based e-commerce logistics firm, per Axios Pro. axios.link/3UyGtvz

• Randa Apparel & Accessories acquired most assets of Untuckit, a brand and retailer of anti-wrinkle shirts for men that was backed by firms like Bond Capital, Clearco, Fifth Wall, and Kleiner Perkins. axios.link/4cshf8l

• Thoma Bravo is seeking to sell Foundation Software, a Strongsville, Ohio-based construction software provider that could fetch more than $2b, per Reuters. axios.link/4xDxbx9

More M&A
 

Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios
 

Google won't be forced to spin off its "network" ad business, despite losing an antitrust case in April, a federal judge ruled yesterday.

• PlusAI, a developer of truck self-driving tech that's raised over $500m from VCs, agreed to go public at an implied $800m valuation via a reverse merger with Texas Ventures Acquisition III (Nasdaq: TVA), a SPAC backed by Yorkville Advisors Global. axios.link/3UwRJsw
 
 
Fundraising
 

• CVC Capital Partners raised $10b for its sixth PE secondaries fund. axios.link/4h5UTMq

• Uplift Ventures, a German deep-tech VC firm, raised €100m for its debut fund and added Christian Noske (ex-NGP Capital) as a general partner. axios.link/3SMVnhg
 
 
It's Personnel
 

• Florida's State Board of Administration promoted John Bradley to head of private markets. axios.link/4qQZ1Dt

🚑 Gail Jermyn joined Advent Life Sciences as an IR partner. She previously was with Weight Partners Capital. axios.link/4gzNx3D

• Todd Kornreich joined Davis Polk as a partner in its M&A practice. He previously was with Ropes & Gray. axios.link/4iItS2T

• Playground Global promoted both Rahul Meka and Daniel Yum to partner. axios.link/4gJB7VP

• Tony Shi joined Felicis as an investment partner. He previously was with Pear VC. Felicis also promoted Michelle Delcambre to general partner. felicis.com

• Stephanie Epstein Srulowitz is joining Simpson Thacher & Bartlett as a partner in its investment funds practice. She previously was with Weil Gotshal. axios.link/4gwvXgW
 
 
🌲 Final Numbers
 
Data: Financial Modeling Prep; Chart: Dan Primack/Axios

Elliott Investment Management is lining up against Deutsche Telekom's efforts to merge with American arm T-Mobile US, in which it holds a 55% stake.

  • The activist investor has built a "sizable stake" in Deutsche Telekom, according to Bloomberg, and opposes the deal.

T-Mobile US has around a $200 billion market cap, despite its stock being down 26% over the past year, and a tie-up would create the world's largest mobile operator.
